travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise increased caution in Chile due to crime and civil unrest.
Country Summary: Street crime (e.g., muggings, pick-pocketing, theft) is common in Chile. Rates of violent crime, such as assaults, homicide, carjackings, and residential break-ins, are increasing.
Large-scale demonstrations periodically occur in Santiago and other cities in Chile. Demonstrations can take place with little or no notice, and often result in disruptions to transportation, including public bus and Santiago metro ser

connectivity.simOptions: Entel, Movistar, or WOM prepaid SIMs at airports or phone shops. Need passport. WOM offers best value data plans.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at hotels, cafes, malls, and some public plazas in Santiago. Coverage limited in Patagonia and remote areas.
connectivity.bestOption: WOM prepaid SIM for best data value. Buy at Santiago airport. eSIM via Airalo works well in major cities.

cultural.tipping: 10% at restaurants is customary. Not expected at cafes. Round up for taxis. Tip tour guides CLP 5,000-10,000/day.
cultural.dressCode: Smart casual in Santiago. Casual in beach towns and the south. No specific religious dress codes.
cultural.greetings: One kiss on the right cheek between men-women and women-women. Handshake between men. 'Hola' followed by '¿Cómo estás?' is standard.
taboos: Comparing Chile unfavorably to Argentina (strong rivalry)
Skipping the greeting ritual — always say hello first
Discussing Pinochet unless the other person brings it up
cultural.haggling: Not common. Prices are fixed at stores and restaurants. Some negotiation at artisan markets in tourist areas.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free. UK, EU, Australia, Canada also visa-free. Tourist card issued at entry.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-March (spring/summer). Atacama Desert: year-round. Patagonia: December-February. Ski season: June-August.

hospitals.name: Clínica Las Condes
hospitals.notes: Top private hospital in Chile with international patient services and English-speaking staff.

immediate: Drop, cover, and hold on — Chile has some of the world's strongest earthquakes
If near the coast, immediately move inland and uphill after shaking stops — tsunami risk
Do not use elevators after shaking stops
Stay outdoors if possible — do not return to buildings until safe
after: If tsunami warning issued, stay at elevation until official all-clear
Follow SHOA (tsunami authority) and ONEMI (national emergency office) instructions
Check for gas leaks and structural damage before re-entering buildings
